issue.title: High number of timer interrupts after upgrade to netty 3.6.4

repository.name: netty
repository.description: Netty project - an event-driven asynchronous network application framework

body:
@voiceinsideyou could you please retest with the 3.6.5.Final-SNAPSHOT and let me know if it is fixed:

https://oss.sonatype.org/content/repositories/snapshots/io/netty/netty/3.6.5.Final-SNAPSHOT/netty-3.6.5.Final-20130408.051635-6.jar

Unfortunately it's still spinning; although at least sleepTimeMs isn't always 0 now so perhaps it's a different issue. Now it's always a negative number that seems to just get more and more negative over time. I saw this kind of thing with 3.6.3 while channels were open, however without more familiarity with what the timer is trying to do I'm not sure what condition caused it to stop spinning and start sleeping...
@voiceinsideyou would be possible for you to submit some code that shows the problem ?

This is going to sound rather churlish (it's not intended that way!), however:

```
new HashedWheelTimer().start();
Thread.sleep(1000000);
```

First iteration sleepTimeMs is 0. After that sleepTimeMs just gets more and more negative and never hits the Thread.sleep().

I think the problem now is line 217 (and possibly other places) - doesn't this need to be unit.toNanos() since you're later adding it to a nanos-based startTime?

For what it's worth, as a test workaround

```
new HashedWheelTimer(100000000L, TimeUnit.MILLISECONDS).start();
```

seems to work normally with a 100 **ms** tickDuration and no CPU spinning.
@voiceinsideyou na it not sounds churlish... Thanks let me check and fix for real!
@voiceinsideyou, the bad exception message was fixed via 44027aebbcc43f2e1ee83c640afc7c042b396862.  Thanks for the heads up.
